Avoid this like the plague!
Nov 2018 • Couples
Stumbled across this restaurant whilst walking across the pedestrian bridge- we thought we had come across the most amazing atmospheric restaurant ever. Little private thatched cabins on stilts with mood lighting.. so lovely and different.
Well, that’s where the pleasantness ended. After being totally ignored by staff when we enquired for the menu (too busy sitting on a bench, one whatsapping, the other over her shoulder looking at her screen and ignoring us totally to the point of absolute awkwardness) it should have rang alarm bells. We finally got seated, there was some problem and seabass was off the menu so we ordered a few other dishes instead, of which half were missing when they came so we had one starter and one main to share, the sides never materialised. I don’t know how they got it so wrong when you are pointing out dishes on a menu! . The staff were no where to be seen after they bought the food.
The food quality though was really good for the tiny amount for what we had.
Now for the offputting part. Throughout the meal we had heard the thatch rustling above us, we naiively thought it was birds. When finishing the meal we saw a rat run across a side beam. I am not saying the restaurant is unhygenic, in this part of the world and to be in such close proximity to the river I guess they are a given, but the kicker was when we waited for the bill 3 large rats ran across a beam above us. We couldn’t get out of there fast enough!

Unique Setting but Mixed Food Results
Jul 2018 • Couples
This was across the pedestrian bridge from where we were staying, and we finally made it a couple nights before leaving. You are literally over the water inside the restaurant - if you can say it has insides. It is a series of thatched roof huts (one for each table) so you have very private dining. Very romantic.
Our initial server looked tired, and apparently there was a shift change or something else because she left and others took her place. Service was good, but not extraordinary.
We started with snail and fried tofu and both were delicious. (Only my second time eating snail, I think.) Then I ordered grilled squid and it also was delicious. We were doing well. My wife ordered egg fish (small whole fish fried - when you bite into them they have eggs inside that you eat as well). These were pretty good, but I was starting to feel full.
We debated what else to order and decided to try the field mouse, but they were out! Then we considered ostrich, but she chose grilled crab. When it arrived, I didn't recognize it. I tasted it, and it had an overpowering taste of liver. There was some pork in it as well, according to my wife, but the crab flavor was nowhere to be found. We couldn't finish it, and that was a disappointment to the entire meal.
Overall an interesting place to visit.

Nice & big idyllic place
Nov 2017 • Friends
Went there for dinner in group of 6 persons and we were pleasantly surprised by the size of the place. There are huts of different sizes catered for different number of people dining there.

The wooden huts are built over water and a single wooden boardwalk leads to the various huts. One note of caution if you are bringing young kids there: do not let them play or run along the boardwalk as the wooden railings on both sides are pretty low. There is a big possibility of them falling over the railings and into the water. Also recommend for you to walk slowly and carefully if you are tipsy after a few drinks during dinner.

The menu has both English and Vietnamese descriptions of the dishes. The quality of food is above average. We ordered some seafood dishes and a beef hotpot. 

The bill was also quite reasonable as we expected it to much higher. Good experience overall.
